transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Raj (Veridian Eng Lead), Marta (Veridian DevOps), Tom (PM), Anika (Security)

Summary (auto): quick run through of access gating, bench numbers from last 24h trial, checklist for staging gateway, and clarifying security/KMS handoff. Plan to run a longer stress window once staging creds are in place.

[00:00] Samir (AE): okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call, uh we have Samir, Lena, Priya from Redwood, and Raj, Marta, Tom and Anika from Veridian. does that look right?
[00:10] Raj: yep, that's us, thanks.
[00:12] Marta: yep, hi all.
[00:14] Samir: great. agenda is lightweight today: onboarding status, gateway cred handoff, brief perf notes from the last 24 hour smoke, and security/KMS check.
[00:22] Tom (PM): sounds good. main thing for us is making sure the staging environment mimics production enough to validate the fallback behavior and cost numbers.
[00:32] Lena (SE): yeah, and just to set expectations, our small smoke yesterday used the rdl-moon-7b variant and we saw tail latency spikes at around 1% of requests when sequence lengths hit ~1,200 tokens. so that's probably attributable to batching behavior and the default token cutoff.
[00:48] Raj: sorry, rdl-moon-7b? I thought you were running the 13B that we discussed.
[00:52] Lena: ah, yes, for the initial smoke we used the 7B because it's faster to iterate, we have results for the 13B too but it's still uploading. the 13B (rawmond-13B? sorry that name got mangled in the notes) showed slightly higher median latency but similar p95 once batching was tuned.
[01:12] Marta: for staging we really need the same quant/profile as prod. can you confirm the quantized artifacts will match?
[01:20] Lena: good question. the build we've pushed is INT8 quant for that model family; there may be a small difference vs your on-prem quant profile. we can produce a matching artifact if you want — that would require a short recompile step and we'll coordinate.
[01:36] Anika (Security): on the security side, we need to validate KMS integration and ensure audit logs flow to our SIEM; also SSO via SAML, not OIDC. is SAML supported in the staging control plane?
[01:48] Priya (CSM): we have SAML for Dedicated and Private deployments; for the hosted plane there's limited SAML support. for your pilot, since you prefer VPC/private control plane, SAML will be available.
[02:02] Anika: okay, please send the exact SAML metadata fields we need.
[02:06] Samir: action — we will drop the SAML metadata and a quick KMS checklist in the thread after the call.
[02:12] [02:15] Raj: quick question on gateway creds — Marta mentioned earlier some trouble with DNS mapping to the staging gateway. any blockers?
[02:20] Marta: yeah so we tried to swap in the gateway cert but our internal CA chain looked different and the handshake failed. i can share the openssl debug output but we need the cert in PEM bundle with the intermediate.
[02:34] Samir: understood. lena, can you confirm the format we expect?
[02:38] Lena: yep, PEM bundle with full chain, and we also support PKCS12 if your infra prefers it. i'll post an example.
[02:46] Marta: when you post, can you also include the expected SANs? we had an issue where the hostnames didn't line up with our internal routing.
[02:54] Samir: yes, we'll provide exact SAN list and a curl example.
[03:01] Tom: on the benching side, can you summarise the throughput/latency numbers from the last run? i saw a spreadsheet but it's a little dense.
[03:08] Lena: sure i can do a short summary: 24 hour smoke with bursty traffic (2-3 qps average, peaks to 12 qps) - median latency for the 7B was ~150ms token generation (this is token gen time not end-to-end), p95 around 520ms, p99 in the 1.2s range on the heavier sequences. inference cost per 1k tokens on that instance profile is about $X. for the 13B the median shifted to ~220ms and p95 to ~650ms but again that's with default batching; we can lower p99 by tightening max batch window but that increases median slightly.
[03:50] Raj: what about KV cache and prefix caching? we expect longer conversations and don't want to hit full recompute each time.
[03:58] Lena: good, we enabled prefix/KV caching in staging — although we noticed cache warmup takes some requests; priming strategy helps. if a node gets evicted there's a fallback to rehydrate from the full context or to a smaller model variant. this is the preconfigured fallback policy we mentioned: try same model, if unavailable fall back to an unquantized variant, then to a smaller size.
[04:20] Marta: fallback is fine as long as it's logged and we can correlate on the request id. the audit trail is key.
[04:27] Priya: logs include request id and model variant; we'll ensure log retention meets your compliance needs.
[04:33] Anika: retention window? we need at least 90 days of request-level metadata for audits.
[04:38] Samir: we can offer 90 days as an add-on, default is 30. we'll document that in the security pack.
[04:44] [05:00] Tom: timeline question — when will staging be gated green for us to run a 48 hour stress?
[05:05] Samir: if Marta can confirm VPC peering and upload the gateway cert today or tomorrow, we can provision the staging gateway in 24 hours. then we recommend a short smoke and then the 48h stress in 48-72 hours. so earliest is around Friday if creds land tomorrow.
[05:22] Marta: i can aim for tomorrow morning, but i also have to get the infra team to open two firewall ports; that's on me.
[05:28] Raj: i'll help coordinate with infra.
[05:30] Anika: on KMS, our key admin needs the exact IAM permissions list to create the key policy. can you share that?
[05:37] Lena: yes, we'll share the minimal IAM statements and a sample key policy. also note we support HSM-backed keys if you require.
[05:44] Anika: HSM would be preferred but we need to weigh cost. for pilot we'll go with KMS-backed and evaluate HSM for long term.
[05:55] [06:10] Samir: quick note on SLOs — i know product wants p95 under 700ms for typical queries. we'll put together a proposal for batch windows, token caps, and fallback thresholds to meet that.
[06:22] Tom: important to include cost delta if we tighten batch windows; we need to present that to the finance sponsor.
[06:29] Samir: understood, we'll include a small delta table.
[06:33] [06:40] Raj: any concerns about data residency? our EU patients data can't leave region.
[06:45] Priya: for private we can pin region; we also support per-tenant routing to keep traffic in EU region. we'll note that in the infra checklist.
[06:54] Anika: and encryption in transit and at rest?
[06:57] Lena: TLS in transit, and at rest with KMS-managed keys. some metadata logs we can encrypt with your key if needed.
[07:06] Marta: small gotcha — when we turned up the initial proxy, internal requests took an extra 80ms due to SNAT, can you recommend a routing approach to avoid hairpinning?
[07:16] Lena: yes, we recommend using policy-based routing and advertising the staging subnet in the peering so traffic doesn't hairpin through the NAT gateway — we'll provide a diagram.
[07:28] [07:45] Tom: ok, to close — who is owning the run of the 48h stress and the pass/fail criteria?
[07:52] Samir: Redwood will provision and monitor, but Veridian will execute the workload and share telemetry. pass/fail criteria: no more than 1% error rate, p95 below 700ms for the sample set we agree on, and no secret leakage or audit failures.
[08:08] Raj: sounds fair. we'll add the exact traffic mix to the shared sheet.
[08:14] Priya: i'll set up a follow-up security deep-dive invite for next Wednesday and add tasks to the playbook.
[08:22] Anika: please add our security lead in the invite (i'll DM the address).
[08:26] Samir: action recap: i'll post SAML/KMS checklist, Lena will post PEM cert example and SANs, Marta will confirm peering and certs, Raj will coordinate infra, and we'll schedule the 48h stress window once staging gateway is up.
[08:44] Tom: one last thing — can you add a note about model-variant fallbacks in the runbook? we want explicit mapping e.g., 13B -> 7B -> 3B if under memory pressure.
[08:52] Lena: will do, and i'll include explicit model names and the expected quality delta.
[08:56] Samir: perfect. thanks everyone, see you at the security deep dive next week.
[09:00] Meeting ended.

Notes on quality: transcription has occasional name mangles (rawmond for rdl-moon), some punctuation oddities. speakers sometimes overlap so speaker labels approximate.
